agenda-y-horarios.body:
# Agenda & schedules

The **Agenda** is your master calendar. Every session, retreat, and event lives here — with its date, time, location, capacity, and assigned resources.

---

## The global agenda view

Go to **Agenda** in the sidebar to see all scheduled sessions across all experiences. You can filter by:
- Date range
- Experience
- Location
- Status (active, cancelled, full)

This is your day-to-day operational view.

---

## Creating a schedule

1. Go to **Agenda** and click **New schedule**, or open a specific experience and add a schedule from within it.
2. Fill in the details:
   - **Experience** — Which experience this session belongs to.
   - **Date and time** — When it starts (and ends, if applicable).
   - **Capacity** — Maximum number of attendees.
   - **Location** — Where it takes place.
   - **Resources** — Instructor(s) and any equipment needed.
3. Set the status to **Active**.
4. Save.

---

## Schedule status

| Status    | What it means                                          |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Active    | Open for booking — clients can reserve their spot      |
| Full      | Capacity reached — no more bookings accepted           |
| Cancelled | Session was cancelled — all tickets are invalidated    |
| Completed | Session has already taken place                        |

The system automatically marks a session as **Full** when all spots are taken. You don't need to do this manually.

---

## Editing a schedule

You can edit a schedule at any time — update the time, increase capacity, change the location. If the session already has bookings, clients with tickets won't be notified automatically; you'll need to do that separately if needed.

---

## Recurring sessions

If you run the same session every week (e.g., Monday yoga at 9 AM), you'll need to create each instance separately. Consider creating them in bulk for the month ahead so clients can plan and book in advance.

---

## Viewing attendees

Click any schedule entry to open it. Inside you'll find the full attendee list — everyone who has a ticket for that session.

---

## Cancelling a session

See *Use case: Handling a cancellation* for the full step-by-step guide to cancelling a session and notifying attendees.

clientes.body:
# Clients

The **Clients** section is a directory of everyone who has registered or made a purchase through OMZONE.

---

## Finding a client

1. Go to **Clients** in the sidebar.
2. Use the search bar to find by name, email, or phone number.

---

## What's in a client profile

Click any client to open their profile:

- **Personal info** — Name, email, phone.
- **Active passes** — Which passes they currently have and how many sessions remain.
- **Order history** — Every purchase they've made.
- **Active tickets** — Upcoming reservations with QR codes.
- **Activity log** — A timestamped record of notable actions on their account.

---

## Editing a client's info

Administrators can update a client's name and phone number from their profile. Email addresses are used for login and can't be changed from this view — contact the OMZONE support team if a client needs their email updated.

---

## A client's passes and balance

If a client asks "how many sessions do I have left on my pass?", this is where you find out:
1. Open their profile.
2. Go to **Active passes**.
3. You'll see each pass with its remaining balance and expiry date.

---

## Helping a client with a ticket

If a client can't find their ticket or needs it resent:
1. Open their profile.
2. Find the order in question.
3. Open the order and click **Resend confirmation**.

---

## Exporting client data

Use the **Export** button (if available) to download client records. Useful for newsletters, outreach, or CRM tools.

complementos.body:
# Add-ons

Add-ons are optional extras that clients can include when they book. Think of a massage after a yoga session, a pre-retreat kit, shuttle service, or a private coaching session.

---

## Creating an add-on

1. Go to **Add-ons** in the sidebar.
2. Click **New add-on**.
3. Fill in the details:
   - **Name** — What the add-on is called (e.g., "Post-session massage").
   - **Description** — A short explanation of what it includes.
   - **Price** — What it costs.
   - **Currency** — MXN or USD.
4. Save the add-on.

---

## Attaching an add-on to an experience

Creating an add-on doesn't automatically link it to anything. You need to connect it to one or more experiences:

1. Open the experience you want to add it to.
2. Go to the **Add-ons** section within the experience.
3. Select the add-on(s) you want to offer.
4. Save.

Now clients will see these add-ons as options during checkout.

---

## Add-on availability

Add-ons can be:
- **Optional** — Clients choose whether to include them.
- **Required** — Less common, but possible for experiences where an extra is mandatory.

---

## Managing existing add-ons

From the **Add-ons** list you can:
- Edit the name, description, or price of any add-on.
- Toggle it active or inactive.
- See which experiences it's linked to.

---

## Price changes

Like experience prices, changing an add-on price only affects future bookings. Existing orders keep the price they were charged.

# Settings

The **Settings** section is where you configure the platform-wide behavior of OMZONE — notifications, branding, cancellation policies, and more.

> Only Administrators have access to Settings. Operators see this section as read-only or not at all.

---

## What you can configure

### Business information
- Business name, logo, and contact details.
- These appear on emails, tickets, and the public site footer.

### Notifications
Configure which automatic emails are sent and when:
- Booking confirmation
- Booking reminder (e.g., 24 hours before the session)
- Cancellation notice
- Pass expiry reminder

For each notification you can customize the message template.

### Cancellation policy
Define the default cancellation and refund policy:
- How many hours in advance a client can cancel.
- Whether refunds are automatic or require manual approval.

### Checkout settings
- Which currencies are accepted.
- Whether clients can pay in installments (if supported by your payment processor).
- Any checkout-level discounts or promo codes.

### Users and access
Manage accounts for your team:
- Create, edit, and deactivate admin and operator accounts.
- See the last time each user logged in.

---

## Changing settings carefully

Some settings affect every new transaction going forward. For example, changing the cancellation policy won't retroactively change anything for orders that already exist — but it will affect all new bookings.

If you're unsure about the impact of a change, make it during off-peak hours and test with a controlled booking first.

experiencias.body:
# Experiences

Experiences are the heart of OMZONE. Everything else — pricing, schedules, tickets, publications — connects back to an experience.

---

## Types of experiences

| Type              | What it is                                                        |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Session           | A recurring class or event (yoga, meditation, breathwork)         |
| Immersion         | A deeper, longer single-day experience with a specific focus      |
| Retreat           | Multi-day program, often with lodging included                    |
| Stay              | Extended residential experience                                   |
| Private Event     | Custom experience for a group — booked by request                 |

---

## Creating a new experience

1. Go to **Experiences** in the sidebar.
2. Click **New experience**.
3. Fill in the basic info:
   - **Internal name** — Your reference only. Clients never see this.
   - **Public name** — What clients see on the site.
   - **Type** — Session, Immersion, Retreat, Stay, or Private Event.
   - **Short description** — A 2-3 line summary that appears in listings.
   - **Full description** — The detailed description for the experience page.
4. Click **Save**.

---

## Experience status

| Status  | What it means                                        |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Draft   | Only visible to admins — not on the public site      |
| Active  | Visible on the public site, available to book        |
| Paused  | Hidden from the public temporarily                   |
| Archived| No longer active — kept for historical records       |

> An experience won't appear on the public site until its status is **Active** and it has at least one active price and one active publication.

---

## Sale mode

The **Sale mode** controls how clients book the experience:

- **Direct purchase** — Client selects a date/time and pays immediately.
- **Request** — Client fills in a request form. You review and confirm (or quote) before payment.
- **Pass only** — The experience can only be booked using a pass, not purchased individually.

---

## Editing an experience

Click any experience in the list to open it. From there you can update any field, change the status, or navigate to its pricing, schedule, add-ons, and linked publications.

---

## Deleting vs. archiving

Avoid deleting experiences that have orders or tickets attached to them — this can affect historical records. Use **Archive** instead to hide the experience without losing the data.

multimedia.body:
# Media

The **Media** library is where all your photos and files live. Any image you want to use in a publication — cover photos, instructor portraits, gallery images — is uploaded here first.

---

## Uploading files

1. Go to **Media** in the sidebar.
2. Click **Upload** or drag and drop files onto the upload area.
3. Supported formats: **JPG, PNG, WebP**
4. Maximum file size: **10 MB** per file.
5. The file appears in the library once uploaded.

---

## Organizing media

Files are organized by upload date by default. You can also:
- Search by filename.
- Filter by type.
- See which publications each file is used in.

---

## Using media in publications

When you add an image block or set a cover photo in a publication:
1. A file picker opens.
2. Browse or search the media library.
3. Click the image you want to use.

You don't need to re-upload the same image every time — once it's in the library, you can reuse it anywhere.

---

## Image quality tips

The quality of your photos directly affects how professional the site looks. Some guidelines:

| Good photos                                | Photos to avoid                             |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| Natural light, clear subjects              | Dark, blurry, or grainy images              |
| Authentic moments from sessions            | Generic stock photos                        |
| Horizontal (landscape) for covers          | Heavily filtered or over-edited             |
| Minimum 1200px wide for cover images       | Screenshots from a phone at low resolution  |

---

## Deleting media

You can delete files from the library if they're no longer needed. Before deleting, check whether the file is being used in any active publications — removing it will leave a broken image in that publication.

ordenes.body:
# Orders

An **order** is the record of a purchase. Every time a client pays for an experience, a package, or a pass, an order is created.

---

## The orders list

Go to **Orders** in the sidebar to see all purchases. You can filter by:
- Date range
- Status
- Client name or email
- Experience

---

## Order statuses

| Status    | What it means                                                 |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Pending   | Payment was started but not completed                         |
| Completed | Payment confirmed — tickets have been generated               |
| Cancelled | Order was cancelled (by client or admin)                      |
| Refunded  | Payment was returned to the client                            |

---

## What's inside an order

Click any order to open it. You'll see:
- **Client** — Who made the purchase and their contact info.
- **Items** — What they bought, at what price, with which add-ons.
- **Payment details** — Amount, payment method, date.
- **Tickets** — The tickets generated for this order (with their QR codes).
- **Activity log** — A timestamped history of every action taken on this order.

---

## Price snapshots

Orders store the **exact price** the client paid at the time of purchase. Even if you later change the price of an experience, the order will always show the original amount.

This is intentional — it gives you a reliable sales history.

---

## Cancelling an order

1. Open the order.
2. Click **Cancel order**.
3. Choose what to do with the tickets (cancel them, or move them to another date).
4. If a refund applies, the system will prompt you for the refund details.

---

## Exporting orders

Use the **Export** button (if available) to download a spreadsheet of orders for a given date range. Useful for accounting and reporting.

# Panel summary

The **Summary** is the first thing you see when you open the admin panel. It gives you a quick pulse check on what's happening today.

---

## What's on the dashboard

### Today's sessions
A list of all scheduled sessions for today — with start times, locations, and how many spots are filled.

### Recent orders
The last few purchases made on the platform. Click any order to open its full detail.

### Recent activity
A log of the most recent actions across the platform: new bookings, ticket validations, content updates.

### Quick stats
At a glance numbers like:
- Total active clients
- Sessions scheduled this week
- Orders in the last 7 days

---

## Using the dashboard day to day

The dashboard is your starting point each day. A good morning routine:

1. Check **Today's sessions** — anything unusual? Is everything staffed?
2. Scan **Recent orders** — any pending payments or issues?
3. Look at **Recent activity** — anything that needs your attention?

From here you can jump to any section using the sidebar.

---

## The dashboard doesn't replace reports

The dashboard shows recent activity — it's not a full analytics tool. For deeper data (revenue trends, best-selling experiences, client retention), use the export options available in the Orders and Clients sections.

paquetes-y-pases.body:
# Packages & Passes

Packages and passes let you sell multiple sessions in a single purchase, often at a better price than buying each one individually. They're a powerful tool for building client loyalty and recurring revenue.

---

## Packages vs. passes — what's the difference?

| Feature          | Package                                | Pass                                       |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| How it works     | Fixed number of sessions purchased together | Access to sessions (by count or time period) |
| Flexibility      | Tied to specific experiences           | Can cover a range of compatible experiences |
| Example          | "10 Pilates sessions"                  | "Monthly unlimited access" or "20-session pass" |

---

## Creating a package

1. Go to **Packages & Passes** in the sidebar.
2. Click **New package**.
3. Fill in:
   - **Name** — What clients will see.
   - **Description** — Who it's for and what it includes.
   - **Number of sessions** — How many sessions are included.
   - **Compatible experiences** — Which experiences can be used with this package.
   - **Price** — The total price of the package.
   - **Validity** — How many days the client has to use all sessions (from purchase date).
4. Set the status to **Active**.
5. Save.

---

## Creating a pass

1. Click **New pass**.
2. Fill in:
   - **Name** — e.g., "Unlimited Monthly Pass".
   - **Type** — By sessions (fixed number) or by time period (unlimited within a date range).
   - **Compatible experiences** — Which experiences it covers.
   - **Price** — What it costs.
   - **Expiry** — Number of days, or a specific end date.
3. Activate and save.

---

## How clients use a package or pass

When a client with an active pass or package books a compatible experience, the system automatically detects it at checkout and offers the option to use their pass instead of paying again. One session is deducted from their balance.

---

## Monitoring usage

From each package or pass entry, you can see:
- How many have been sold.
- For each active pass: who holds it, how many sessions remain, and when it expires.

---

## Pass expiry

When a pass expires, unused sessions are forfeited. The system will not automatically extend a pass — the client needs to purchase a new one. Consider sending a reminder notification before expiry (see **Settings → Notifications**).

precios.body:
# Pricing

Each experience can have one or more price levels — general admission, member pricing, early bird, group rates, and so on.

---

## Adding a price to an experience

1. Open the experience.
2. Go to the **Pricing** section.
3. Click **Add price**.
4. Fill in the fields:
   - **Name** — What this price tier is called (e.g., "General", "Early Bird").
   - **Amount** — The price number.
   - **Currency** — MXN or USD.
   - **Description** — Optional note about what's included or who it's for.
5. Toggle it **Active**.
6. Save.

---

## Multiple price tiers

You can have as many price tiers as you need. At checkout, clients see all active tiers and choose the one that applies to them.

**Example:**
- General — $800 MXN
- Members — $600 MXN
- Early bird (limited spots) — $650 MXN

---

## Price status

| Status   | What it means                                    |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Active   | Visible at checkout — clients can select it      |
| Inactive | Hidden — clients won't see this price            |

Deactivating a price doesn't affect orders that already used it.

---

## Changing a price

You can edit a price at any time. **The change only affects future purchases** — existing orders always keep the price that was in effect when the client paid.

This is intentional. It means you can update prices freely without worrying about retroactively changing what a client paid.

---

## Removing a price

If you no longer want to offer a price tier, set it to **Inactive** rather than deleting it. This preserves the record for any past orders that used it.

---

## Prices and passes

If you have pass-based pricing, passes are configured separately under **Packages & Passes**. A pass can give access to experiences that also have individual prices — or it can be the only way to book a particular experience (using the **Pass only** sale mode).

publicaciones.body:
# Publications

A **publication** is the editorial layer of an experience — the story, the photos, the descriptions, and all the content that clients read on the public site.

Publications are intentionally separate from the commercial setup (pricing, schedules). This lets you update the storytelling without touching the business logic, and vice versa.

---

## Creating a publication

1. Go to **Publications** in the sidebar.
2. Click **New publication**.
3. Fill in the basics:
   - **Title** — The public-facing title.
   - **Summary** — A short teaser (2-3 lines) that appears in listings.
   - **Cover image** — The main photo clients see first.
   - **Experience** — Link this publication to the experience it represents.
4. Save.

---

## Building the content

Once the publication is created, you build its content using **sections and blocks**. Each section is a content area (hero image, text block, gallery, about the instructor, etc.).

See **Sections & Blocks** for details on how to structure a publication.

---

## Publication status

| Status    | What it means                                             |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Draft     | Only visible to admins — not on the public site           |
| Active    | Live on the public site                                   |
| Scheduled | Will go live at a specific date/time                      |
| Archived  | No longer active — kept for reference                     |

---

## Updating a publication

You can edit a publication at any time. Changes go live immediately (if the publication is active), so be deliberate about edits you make while a session is actively booking.

---

## Publications vs. experiences

| Publications                               | Experiences                                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| Tell the story — who, why, what to expect  | Define the product — price, dates, capacity |
| Photos, narratives, instructor bios        | Sale mode, schedule, add-ons                |
| Can exist standalone (blog-style articles) | Can exist without a publication             |
| Multiple publications can link to one experience | One experience links to one active pub  |

---

## SEO and discoverability

Publications support:
- **Page title** and **meta description** — for search engine results
- **Canonical URL** — to avoid duplicate content issues
- Structured data is generated automatically for linked experiences

Keep titles and descriptions unique across all publications for best search performance.

recursos.body:
# Resources

A **resource** is anything you need in order to run a session: a person (instructor, facilitator), a room (yoga studio, meditation hall), or a piece of equipment (sound bath instruments, massage table).

Resources are assigned to schedules so the system can track availability and prevent double-booking.

---

## Types of resources

| Type      | Examples                                        |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Person    | Instructor, guide, therapist, facilitator       |
| Space     | Main studio, outdoor terrace, retreat room      |
| Equipment | Sound bath set, projector, mats, massage table  |

---

## Creating a resource

1. Go to **Resources** in the sidebar.
2. Click **New resource**.
3. Fill in:
   - **Name** — The instructor's name, room name, or equipment label.
   - **Type** — Person, space, or equipment.
   - **Capacity** — For spaces: maximum number of people. For people: usually 1 (one session at a time).
   - **Description** — Optional bio or notes.
4. Save.

---

## Assigning resources to a schedule

When you create or edit a schedule:
1. Find the **Resources** field.
2. Select the instructor, room, and any equipment needed.
3. Save the schedule.

If a resource is already booked at the same time, the system will warn you before saving.

---

## Resource availability

The system uses resource assignments to prevent conflicts. If you try to schedule two sessions at the same time with the same instructor or in the same room, you'll get a conflict warning.

---

## Instructors on the public site

Resources don't automatically appear on the public site. To feature an instructor's bio and photo:
1. Open the publication linked to the experience.
2. Add an **About the instructor** or **Team** section.
3. Write the bio, upload a photo, and save.

---

## Deactivating a resource

If an instructor leaves or a room is no longer available:
1. Open the resource.
2. Set its status to **Inactive**.

Inactive resources won't appear as options when creating new schedules, but existing schedules that used them are unaffected.

secciones-y-bloques.body:
# Sections & blocks

Publications are built with **sections** — each one is a content area on the page. Inside sections, you add **blocks**: text, images, galleries, call-to-action buttons, and more.

---

## The structure

```
Publication
  └── Section 1 (e.g., Hero)
        ├── Block: Full-width image
        └── Block: Headline + tagline
  └── Section 2 (e.g., About the experience)
        ├── Block: Long-form text
        └── Block: Image grid
  └── Section 3 (e.g., About the instructor)
        ├── Block: Profile image
        └── Block: Bio text
```

---

## Adding a section

1. Open a publication.
2. Scroll to the sections area and click **Add section**.
3. Choose a section template (hero, text + image, gallery, team, etc.) or start blank.
4. Give the section a name for your reference.
5. Save.

---

## Adding blocks to a section

1. Open a section.
2. Click **Add block**.
3. Choose the block type:
   - **Text** — Rich text, headers, lists, links
   - **Image** — Single photo with optional caption
   - **Gallery** — Multiple photos in a grid
   - **Video** — Embedded video
   - **Call to action** — Button that links to a booking or URL
   - **Quote** — Highlighted pull quote
4. Fill in the content.
5. Save.

---

## Reordering sections

Drag sections up or down to change the order they appear on the page.

---

## Reordering blocks within a section

Same thing — drag blocks within a section to reorder them.

---

## Tips for great publications

- **Start strong** — Your first section should immediately answer: "What is this, and why should I care?"
- **Use real photos** — Stock images feel impersonal. Authentic photos of the space and people build trust.
- **Keep text scannable** — Short paragraphs, clear headers, bullet points where it makes sense.
- **One clear CTA** — Don't confuse clients with five different buttons. One "Book now" per page is enough.
- **Mobile first** — Many clients will see this on their phone. Preview it at mobile size before publishing.

solicitudes-de-reserva.body:
# Booking requests

A **booking request** is what happens when a client is interested in an experience but doesn't pay immediately — they send an inquiry first, and you respond with a confirmation or a quote.

This flow is used for private events, group experiences, and any experience where you need to align details before accepting payment.

---

## How requests arrive

When an experience is set to **Request** mode (instead of direct purchase), the **Book now** button becomes **Send a request**. The client fills in:
- Their preferred date(s)
- Number of people
- Special requests or questions

The request lands in your panel with status **Pending**.

---

## Reviewing a request

1. Go to **Booking Requests** in the sidebar.
2. Open any **Pending** request.
3. You'll see the client's details, their message, and what they're asking for.

---

## Responding to a request

You have three options:

### Confirm directly
If everything is clear and you can accommodate the request:
- Click **Confirm**.
- The client receives an email with a payment link.
- Once they pay, a ticket is generated.

### Send a quote
If you need to negotiate price or clarify details:
1. Enter the quoted amount in the **Quoted price** field.
2. Write a message to the client.
3. Click **Send quote**.
4. The client receives the quote by email and can accept it and pay directly from the link.

### Decline
If you can't accommodate the request:
1. Click **Decline**.
2. Optionally write a brief explanation for the client.
3. The client receives a notification that their request wasn't accepted.

---

## Best practice

Try to respond to requests within 24 hours. Clients who don't hear back quickly often move on.

---

## Request statuses

| Status    | What it means                                     |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Pending   | Waiting for your response                         |
| Quoted    | You've sent a quote — waiting for client payment  |
| Confirmed | Client paid — ticket generated                    |
| Declined  | Request was turned down                           |
| Expired   | Client didn't respond to the quote in time        |

tickets.body:
# Tickets

A **ticket** is the entry pass for a specific session. It's generated automatically when an order is completed, and contains a unique QR code that the client presents on the day of the experience.

---

## Finding a ticket

From **Orders**: open any order — its tickets are listed at the bottom.

From **Agenda**: open a schedule and see the full attendee list with one ticket per person.

Searching by client name or email also brings up their tickets.

---

## Ticket statuses

| Status  | What it means                                             |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Active  | Valid — the client can use it to attend                   |
| Used    | Already scanned — client attended the session             |
| Cancelled | The reservation was cancelled                           |
| Expired | The session date passed without the ticket being scanned  |

---

## Validating a ticket

On the day of the session, scan the client's QR code using the validation tool in the panel (or a mobile scanner). The ticket status changes from **Active** to **Used** immediately.

If the QR doesn't scan, look up the client by name or email and validate manually.

---

## Manually changing a ticket's status

If a ticket was scanned incorrectly or needs correction:
1. Open the ticket.
2. Click **Mark as used** (or the appropriate action).
3. The change is recorded in the ticket's activity log with a timestamp.

Use this carefully — ticket status changes are logged and visible.

---

## Cancelling a ticket

1. Open the ticket (or the order it belongs to).
2. Click **Cancel ticket**.
3. The client receives an email notification.
4. If a refund applies, process it from the order.

---

## Resending a ticket

If a client says they didn't receive their ticket:
1. Open the order.
2. Click **Resend confirmation** (or **Resend ticket**).
3. The ticket email is sent again to the client's address.

ubicaciones.body:
# Locations

A **location** is a physical place where your experiences happen — a studio address, an outdoor space, a retreat property, or a partner venue.

---

## Creating a location

1. Go to **Locations** in the sidebar.
2. Click **New location**.
3. Fill in:
   - **Name** — What this place is called (e.g., "Main Studio", "Oceanfront Terrace").
   - **Address** — Full street address.
   - **City** — City name.
   - **Description** — A short description for clients (optional).
   - **Map link** — A Google Maps or similar URL so clients can get directions easily.
   - **Photo** — An image of the space (optional but recommended).
4. Save.

---

## Using locations in schedules

When you create a schedule, you assign a location to it. This tells both your team and your clients exactly where the session takes place.

Clients can see the location name and address on:
- The experience page on the public site
- Their booking confirmation email
- Their ticket

---

## Multiple locations

If you run experiences in different places, each one should have its own location entry. This lets you:
- Filter the agenda by location
- Track capacity per space
- Show clients accurate directions

---

## Editing a location

You can update a location's details at any time. Changes apply to future schedules — past events aren't affected.

---

## Deactivating a location

If you stop using a space, set it to **Inactive**. It won't appear as an option for new schedules, but historical data is preserved.

venta-asistida.body:
# Assisted sale

**Assisted sale** lets you place a purchase on behalf of a client without them needing to go through the public site. It's for walk-ins, phone orders, and situations where a client needs your help completing their booking.

---

## When to use it

- A client shows up in person and wants to pay cash or via a separate payment method.
- A client calls and asks you to reserve a spot for them.
- A client had trouble completing their purchase online and you need to do it for them.
- You want to register attendance at a session that wasn't booked online.

---

## How to place an assisted sale

1. Go to **Assisted Sale** in the sidebar.
2. Find or create the client:
   - Search by name or email.
   - If they're not in the system, you can create them on the spot.
3. Select the experience.
4. Choose the date and time (from available schedules).
5. Select the price tier.
6. Add any extras (add-ons) if needed.
7. Select the payment method (cash, card, bank transfer, etc.).
8. Confirm the sale.

A ticket is generated immediately and linked to the client's account.

---

## Payment methods in assisted sale

Assisted sale supports payment methods that aren't available on the public site:
- Cash
- Bank transfer
- Card on location
- Courtesy (no charge — for complimentary entries)

The payment method is recorded in the order for your accounting records.

---

## The client receives a ticket

Even though the sale was made from the panel, the client still gets a ticket in their portal (if they have an account) and receives a confirmation email.

---

## No account? No problem

If the client doesn't have an account, you can register the sale under a temporary record. If they later create an account with the same email, their purchase history will be linked.

# Handle a cancellation

Cancellations happen. Here's how to handle the most common scenarios cleanly.

---

## Scenario 1 — A client wants to cancel their ticket

When a client asks to cancel their reservation:

1. Go to **Tickets** and find their ticket (search by name, email, or order number).
2. Open the ticket.
3. Review the cancellation policy that applies.
4. Click **Cancel ticket**.
5. Confirm.

The ticket is marked **Cancelled**. The client won't be able to check in with it.

**What about a refund?**
Refunds are handled separately through your payments settings. If a refund is due, process it from the **Orders** section.

---

## Scenario 2 — You need to cancel a specific order

If a client's entire order needs to be cancelled (not just one ticket):

1. Go to **Orders** and find the order.
2. Open it.
3. Click **Cancel order**.
4. Select the reason (if applicable).
5. Confirm.

All tickets in that order are cancelled automatically.

---

## Scenario 3 — You need to cancel an entire session

When circumstances require cancelling a whole scheduled session:

1. Go to **Agenda** and open the session.
2. Click **Cancel session** (or **Archive schedule**).
3. Confirm.

**After cancelling:**
- All tickets for that session are automatically marked as **Cancelled**.
- Affected clients should be notified. Use **Send notification** from the session or contact them manually.
- If refunds are applicable, process them through **Orders**.

---

## Scenario 4 — Rescheduling instead of cancelling

If you want to move a session to a different date rather than cancelling it:

1. **Cancel the original session** (or mark it as moved).
2. **Create a new schedule** with the updated date and time.
3. **Notify clients** — let them know the new date and how to rebook.

> Currently, tickets are tied to specific schedules. Clients need to rebook for the new date rather than having their ticket automatically transferred.

---

## Communicating with clients

When cancelling something, always let the client know:
- **What** was cancelled.
- **Why** (if appropriate).
- **What they should do** — rebook, wait for a refund, contact you.

Use **Send notification** from the relevant order or session, or reach out directly by email.

recuperar-acceso-cliente.body:
# Recover a client's access

One of the most common support situations: a client can't get into their account. Here's how to handle every scenario.

---

## Scenario 1 — "I forgot my password"

**Tell the client:**

1. Go to the OMZONE login page.
2. Click **Forgot your password?**
3. Enter the email address used to create the account.
4. Check their inbox for a password reset email.
5. Follow the link in the email to set a new password.

**If the email doesn't arrive:** See Scenario 2.

---

## Scenario 2 — "I didn't receive the reset email"

**Things to check:**

- **Spam/junk folder** — The email sometimes ends up there.
- **Correct email** — Are they sure they're using the right address? If they've used multiple emails over the years, they might be checking the wrong inbox.
- **Wait a few minutes** — Occasionally emails are slightly delayed.

**If the email is confirmed but still not arriving:**

1. Go to **Clients** in the admin panel.
2. Search for the client's account by email.
3. From the client's profile, you can trigger a password reset or a new confirmation email from your side.

---

## Scenario 3 — "My account seems to be blocked"

1. Go to **Clients** in the admin panel.
2. Find the client and open their profile.
3. Check the account status — if it's disabled or blocked, you can re-enable it from there.
4. Let the client know and ask them to try logging in again.

---

## Scenario 4 — "I don't think I have an account"

It's possible the client made a purchase without realizing they created an account, or their account is under a different email.

**Steps:**

1. Go to **Clients** in the admin panel.
2. Search by their name, email, or phone number.
3. If an account exists, let them know which email to use.
4. If no account exists, they can create one on the login page by clicking **Sign up**.

---

## Scenario 5 — "I want to change my email address"

Clients can't change their email themselves (it's their login identifier). To change it:

1. Go to **Clients** in the admin panel.
2. Find the client.
3. Update the email from the client's profile (if your role allows it).
4. Let the client know the new email is now their login.

> Note: Any orders and tickets already associated with the old email will still appear in the account history.

---

## Quick reference

| Situation                          | Action                                              |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Forgot password                    | Use "Forgot password?" on login page               |
| Reset email not arriving           | Check spam; admin can trigger reset manually        |
| Account blocked                    | Admin re-enables from Clients panel                 |
| Doesn't know which email was used  | Admin searches by name/phone in Clients panel       |
| Wants to change email              | Admin updates email from client's profile           |

# Handle a private event request

Some experiences — private yoga sessions, group events, bachelorette retreats — don't have a fixed price or a standard schedule. Instead, interested clients submit a **booking request** and your team responds with details or a custom quote.

---

## How the request flow works

```
Client submits a request form
        ↓
Request appears in admin panel
        ↓
Your team reviews it
        ↓
You decline, quote, or confirm
        ↓
If confirmed → client receives payment link
        ↓
After payment → ticket is generated
```

---

## Step 1 — Make sure the experience uses request mode

For experiences that should use this flow:

1. Go to **Experiences** and open the experience.
2. In the **Sale mode** field, select *By request*.
3. Save.

Clients will now see a "Request" button instead of "Book now."

---

## Step 2 — Client submits a request

The client fills in the form:
- Preferred date(s)
- Number of attendees
- Any specific needs or notes

They submit. You get a notification.

---

## Step 3 — Review the request

1. Go to **Booking requests** in the admin panel.
2. Click the request to open it.
3. Review the details: who's asking, when, how many people, their notes.

---

## Step 4 — Respond

From the request, you have three options:

### Accept and confirm
- Set the date, time, and final price.
- Add any notes for the client.
- Click **Confirm**.
- The client receives a payment link by email.

### Send a quote
- If you need to propose a custom price or clarify details first.
- Enter your quote and a message.
- Click **Send quote**.
- The client can review and accept.

### Decline
- If you can't accommodate the request.
- Add an optional message explaining why.
- Click **Decline**.
- The client is notified.

---

## Step 5 — Client pays

Once the client receives the payment link:
1. They open the link.
2. They review the details and pay.
3. Payment is processed.
4. A ticket with a QR code is generated automatically.
5. The ticket appears in their portal and is sent by email.

---

## Tracking requests

In **Booking requests**, you can filter by:
- Status (Pending, Confirmed, Declined, Paid)
- Date
- Experience

Use this view to stay on top of all incoming requests and follow up as needed.

vender-un-paquete.body:
# Sell a session package

A **package** bundles several sessions into a single purchase — convenient for clients and great for your recurring revenue.

**Example:** "10-session yoga package — valid for 90 days."

---

## How packages work

1. The client buys the package in one transaction.
2. They receive a pass with a set number of sessions.
3. Each time they book a compatible experience, one session is deducted from their balance.

---

## Step 1 — Plan the package

Before creating it, decide:

- **How many sessions** does the package include?
- **Which experiences** can it be used for?
- **How long is it valid?** (30 days? 90 days? 6 months?)
- **What's the price?** (And is there an early-bird or limited-time offer?)

---

## Step 2 — Create the package

1. Go to **Packages & Passes** in the admin panel.
2. Click **New package**.
3. Fill in:
   - **Name** — What clients will see (e.g., "10-session pass").
   - **Number of sessions** — How many sessions this package includes.
   - **Validity period** — How many days after purchase it's valid.
   - **Compatible experiences** — Which experiences can be booked with this pass.
4. Set the price.
5. Save.

---

## Step 3 — Publish the package

1. Make sure the package is set to **Active**.
2. Create a publication that describes the package (or link it to an existing experience page).
3. Clients will be able to purchase it from the public site.

---

## Step 4 — Test the purchase flow

1. Create a test account (or use an existing client account).
2. Purchase the package on the public site.
3. Confirm:
   - The pass appears in the client's portal under **My passes**.
   - The session count is correct.
   - The expiry date is set correctly.
   - When booking a compatible experience, the system offers to use the pass.

---

## What happens at checkout

When a client with an active pass tries to book a compatible experience:
1. The system detects the pass automatically.
2. It asks: "Use your pass or pay directly?"
3. If they choose the pass, one session is deducted. No charge is made.

---

## Managing active packages

- Go to **Packages & Passes** to see all packages.
- You can edit pricing, extend validity, or deactivate a package at any time.
- Deactivating stops new sales — it doesn't affect passes already purchased.

---

## Monitoring pass usage

In the admin panel, you can see:
- How many sessions each pass holder has left.
- Which experiences they've used their pass for.
- Whether a pass has expired.

# Welcome to OMZONE

OMZONE is a platform for booking and managing wellness experiences — yoga sessions, immersions, retreats, private events, and more.

This documentation is for the people who run OMZONE: administrators, operators, and clients. You won't find code here — just clear, step-by-step guides for everything you need to do.

---

## Who is this documentation for?

| If you are...    | This documentation helps you...                                      |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Administrator    | Manage every aspect of the platform — experiences, sales, settings   |
| Operator         | Handle day-to-day content and operations                             |
| Client           | Understand your portal: tickets, passes, and your profile            |

---

- **Getting Started** — Log in, understand roles, and get a feel for the admin panel
- **Admin Panel** — Everything you can do as an administrator or operator
- **Client Portal** — What clients see and can do after logging in
- **Public Site** — How visitors browse and buy experiences
- **Use Cases** — End-to-end walkthroughs for the most common tasks

If you can't find what you're looking for in these docs, use the search bar at the top, or contact the OMZONE support team directly.

# Roles and permissions

OMZONE has three user roles. Each one has a different level of access to the platform.

---

## The three roles

### Administrator

Full access to everything:
- Create, edit, and delete experiences, pricing, schedules, and content
- Manage orders, tickets, and refunds
- View and manage all clients
- Configure platform settings
- Access all reports and activity logs
- Create and manage operator accounts

**This is the owner or lead manager of the business.**

---

### Operator

Day-to-day access without touching sensitive settings:
- View and manage experiences, schedules, and content
- Manage orders and tickets
- Use the assisted sale tool
- View clients (no sensitive data)
- Cannot change platform settings or financial configurations

**This is a staff member who runs the operation daily.**

---

### Client

Access to their own portal only:
- View their tickets and reservations
- Manage their passes
- Review their purchase history
- Update their personal profile

**This is anyone who has bought or reserved an experience.**

---

## What can each role see?

| Feature                   | Administrator | Operator | Client |
| ------------------------- | :-----------: | :------: | :----: |
| Admin panel               | ✓             | ✓        | —      |
| Manage experiences        | ✓             | ✓        | —      |
| Manage pricing            | ✓             | —        | —      |
| Manage orders & tickets   | ✓             | ✓        | —      |
| Assisted sale             | ✓             | ✓        | —      |
| Platform settings         | ✓             | —        | —      |
| Client portal             | —             | —        | ✓      |
| Own tickets & passes      | —             | —        | ✓      |

---

## How do I know which role I have?

Look at the menu available after you log in:
- If you see the full admin panel with all sections → **Administrator**
- If you see the admin panel but some settings are missing → **Operator**
- If you see your personal portal with tickets and passes → **Client**

---

## Can someone have more than one role?

No. Each account has one role. If you need broader access, an administrator can update your account.

como-explora-un-visitante.body:
# How visitors browse the site

A visitor is someone who arrives at OMZONE without being logged in — a potential client who found you through Google, social media, or word of mouth.

Understanding how they navigate helps you create better publications and experiences.

---

## The typical visitor journey

```
1. Visitor arrives at the site
   (via Google, Instagram, a friend's recommendation)
        ↓
2. Lands on the home page
   (first impression — "what is this place?")
        ↓
3. Browses the experience catalog
   ("what can I actually do here?")
        ↓
4. Opens an experience that catches their eye
   (reads the description, scrolls the photos, checks the price)
        ↓
5. Decides to book
   (clicks "Book now" or "Reserve")
        ↓
6. Prompted to log in or create an account
   (new visitors create one in about 2 minutes)
        ↓
7. Completes checkout
        ↓
8. Receives confirmation email and ticket
```

---

## Where visitors make decisions

### Do I stay or leave?

Visitors decide in the first few seconds whether to keep exploring. Your home page and experience photos carry that weight.

**What helps:** High-quality images, a clear value proposition ("Yoga retreats in Puerto Vallarta"), and a visible call to action.

---

### Am I interested in this experience?

When a visitor opens an experience page, they're asking:
- What exactly will I experience?
- Is this for someone like me?
- How much does it cost?
- When can I go?

**What helps:** A narrative description (not a bullet list of features), real photos, clear pricing, and visible upcoming dates.

---

### Do I trust this place?

Before paying, visitors want to feel confident they're in good hands.

**What helps:** Client testimonials, instructor bios, photos of the team and the space, and a professional, well-maintained site.

---

## Returning visitors

A visitor might save your site and come back later. That means it's important to:
- Keep schedules up to date.
- Publish new experiences regularly.
- Make sure pricing is always visible and correct.

# How the public site is structured

The **public site** is what everyone sees before they log in or create an account. It's your storefront — the first impression for every potential client.

---

## Main pages

### Home

Your brand's first impression. The home page presents who you are, what you offer, and why it matters.

It typically includes:
- A hero section with a striking image or video and a clear call to action.
- A curated selection of featured experiences.
- Editorial sections: benefits, testimonials, moments gallery, your philosophy.
- A footer with contact info, social links, and legal pages.

---

### Experience catalog

A browsable listing of all active experiences. Visitors can filter by type and explore what's available.

---

### Experience page

When a visitor clicks on an experience, they land on its detail page. This is where they read the full story, see photos, review pricing, and start the booking process.

→ See **Experience page** for a full breakdown.

---

### Additional pages

Depending on your setup, the site may also include:
- **About** — Your story and philosophy.
- **Contact** — A form for general inquiries.
- **Blog / Articles** — Editorial content published as standalone articles.

---

## The navigation bar

At the top of every page:

- Main navigation links.
- A **Log in** / **Sign up** button.

---

## The footer

At the bottom:
- Contact information.
- Social media links.
- Quick links to legal pages.

---

## What drives the public site content

# The checkout flow

Here's the full journey from "I want this" to "I have my ticket."

---

## Step 1 — They choose the experience

The client is on an experience page and clicks the main action button: **Book now**, **Purchase**, or **Request** — depending on how the experience is set up.

---

## Step 2 — They pick a date and time (if applicable)

For experiences with available schedules, the client selects when they want to attend.

Only sessions with open spots appear as options.

---

## Step 3 — They choose a price tier (if there are multiple)

Some experiences offer different price levels:
- General admission
- Member price
- Early bird rate

The client selects the one that applies to them.

---

## Step 4 — They add extras (optional)

If the experience has add-ons available (e.g., a post-session massage, transport, a starter kit), the client can select them here.

---

## Step 5 — They log in or create an account

If the client isn't logged in, they're prompted to:
- **Log in** to an existing account, or
- **Create an account** with their name, email, and password.

Creating an account takes about two minutes.

---

## Step 6 — They review and pay

The client sees a summary of what they're buying:
- Experience name and details
- Date and time
- Itemized pricing
- Total

They enter their payment details and confirm.

> Payments are processed securely. No card data is stored in OMZONE.

---

## Step 7 — Confirmation and ticket

After a successful payment:
1. A confirmation screen appears.
2. A confirmation email is sent to their inbox.
3. The ticket with its QR code appears in their portal under **My tickets**.

---

## The request flow (private experiences)

Some experiences skip the direct purchase and use a **request** flow instead:

1. Client fills in the request form (preferred dates, group size, notes).
2. The OMZONE team receives the request in the admin panel.
3. The team replies with a confirmation or a custom quote.
4. If the client accepts, they receive a payment link.
5. After payment, the ticket is generated.

→ See **Booking requests** in the admin section for how to handle these from your side.

# The experience page

The **experience page** is where visitors decide to book. It combines two things: the **narrative** (the publication) and the **commercial details** (the experience itself).

---

## What the visitor sees

### At the top
- **Experience name** — The public name you set.
- **Cover image** — The main photo.
- **Short description** — Your 2-3 line summary.
- **Starting price** — The lowest active price.
- **Action button** — "Book now", "Reserve", or "Request" depending on the sale mode.

### In the body
- **Editorial content** — The sections and blocks from the linked publication: text, photos, gallery, instructor bio.
- **Full description** — The longer description of the experience.
- **Available dates** — If there are active schedules, they appear here for clients to choose from.
- **Pricing** — All active price tiers.
- **Add-ons** — Optional extras available for this experience.

---

## Where each element comes from

| What the visitor sees        | Where it comes from in the admin panel                    |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Experience name              | Experience → Info → Public name                           |
| Cover image                  | Experience → Info → Cover image                           |
| Short description            | Experience → Info → Short description                     |
| Pricing                      | Experience → Pricing → Active price tiers                 |
| Available dates              | Experience → Schedules (or Global agenda)                 |
| Editorial content            | Linked publication → Sections                             |
| Add-ons                      | Experience → Linked add-ons                               |

---

## What happens when something is missing

- **No active price** — The booking button won't appear or shows "Not available."
- **No schedules** — The date picker won't appear.
- **No linked publication** — The page shows only basic info with no editorial content.

---

## Making the most of an experience page

To maximize bookings:

1. **Compelling cover photo** — First visual impression.
2. **Short description that hooks** — The first two lines should make someone want to read more.
3. **Visible, clear pricing** — Visitors shouldn't have to hunt for the price.
4. **Up-to-date schedules** — Nothing discourages a visitor more than finding no available dates.
5. **Rich editorial content** — The more story and emotion you convey, the easier the decision.

# My passes

Passes let you attend multiple sessions without buying each one individually. If you practice regularly, a pass is the most convenient (and usually the most affordable) way to book.

---

## Getting there

From your portal, click **My passes** in the menu.

---

## Types of passes

| Type             | How it works                                                           |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Session pass     | You bought a set number of sessions — one is deducted per attendance.  |
| Time-based pass  | Unlimited access for a defined period (weekly, monthly, etc.).         |

---

## Your pass list

You'll see all your passes — active and expired. Each one shows:

- **Pass name** — What it covers.
- **Remaining balance** — How many sessions you have left (for session passes).
- **Expiry date** — How long it's valid.
- **Status** — Active, expired, or used up.

---

## Using a pass to book

When you book a compatible experience:

1. At checkout, the system detects your active pass automatically.
2. It asks if you'd like to use the pass instead of paying.
3. Confirm, and one session is deducted from your balance.

---

## Usage history

Inside each pass you can see a full log of when and which experiences you used it for.

---

## Common pass questions

**Can I use my pass for any experience?**
Only experiences that are compatible with your pass. Each pass specifies which experiences it covers.

**What happens when my pass expires with sessions still left?**
Unused sessions are forfeited at expiry. Make sure to use your pass before it runs out.

**Can I have more than one pass at a time?**
Yes. Each pass is independent and you can hold multiple at once.

**How do I renew my pass?**
Purchase a new one from the **Explore** section before your current pass expires.

**Can I transfer my pass to someone else?**
No. Passes are personal and non-transferable.

# My tickets & reservations

This is where you'll find all your tickets — both upcoming and past.

---

## Getting there

From your portal, click **My tickets** in the menu.

---

## What is a ticket?

A **ticket** is your digital proof of reservation. It has a unique QR code that you present on the day of the experience so the OMZONE team can check you in.

---

## The ticket list

Your tickets are sorted with the soonest upcoming ones at the top. Each ticket shows:

- The name of the experience.
- The date and time.
- The venue.
- The ticket status.

---

## Ticket statuses

| Status    | What it means                                             |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Active    | Your ticket is valid — use it the day of the experience   |
| Used      | You attended — your ticket was scanned                    |
| Cancelled | Your reservation was cancelled                            |
| Expired   | The session date passed without the ticket being used     |

---

## Viewing your QR code

1. Click the ticket you want to open.
2. The QR code appears on screen.
3. Show it to the OMZONE staff on arrival — they'll scan it.

> No need to print it. Showing it on your phone is perfectly fine.

---

## Downloading your ticket

If you want to save a copy:

1. Open the ticket.
2. Tap **Download** (if available).
3. It saves as an image to your device.

---

## Lost your ticket?

Don't worry. As long as your account exists, your tickets do too. Just log in, go to **My tickets**, and open the one you need.

If you're having trouble finding it, the OMZONE team can look it up for you using your name and email.

---

## Reservations without a ticket

Some experiences don't generate a ticket — instead, you receive a **booking confirmation**. This is normal for experiences that don't require QR check-in.

# What is the client portal?

The **client portal** is your personal space on OMZONE. It's different from the public site — this area is only for you, and you access it with your registered account.

---

## What the portal is for

From your portal you can:

- View your active tickets and upcoming reservations.
- Show or download the QR code for your tickets.
- Check your pass balance and expiry dates.
- Review your full purchase history.
- Update your personal details and password.

In short: it's where you manage everything you've purchased through OMZONE.

---

## Getting to the portal

1. Go to the OMZONE website.
2. Click **Log in**.
3. Enter your email and password.
4. You'll be taken directly to your portal.

> If you don't have an account yet, you can create one from the login screen.

---

## The portal menu

Once you're in, the menu has these sections:

| Section          | What it's for                                              |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Explore          | Browse experiences available to book                       |
| My dashboard     | A quick summary of your recent bookings and activity       |
| My tickets       | Active and past tickets                                    |
| My passes        | Your active passes and remaining balance                   |
| My profile       | Your personal details and password                         |

---

## Can I buy from the portal?

Yes. From the **Explore** section you can browse all available experiences and purchase new ones directly from your account.

---

## Can I access the admin panel?

No. The client portal is completely separate from the admin panel. As a client, you only see and manage what belongs to your own account.

validar-ticket.body:
# Using your ticket on the day

The day has arrived. Here's exactly what to do to get checked in without a hitch.

---

## Before you leave home

1. **Confirm the time and location** — It's on your ticket and in your confirmation email.
2. **Open your ticket** — Log into the portal, go to **My tickets**, and open today's ticket. The QR code will be on screen.
3. **Charge your phone** — Make sure you have enough battery to show the QR.

---

## When you arrive

1. Head to the check-in desk or reception area.
2. When prompted, show the QR code on your phone to the OMZONE staff.
3. They'll scan it with their device.
4. You'll see a confirmation in seconds.
5. You're in. Enjoy!

---

## Opening your ticket quickly

1. Open the OMZONE portal (if you're already logged in, it's instant).
2. Go to **My tickets**.
3. Tap today's ticket.
4. The QR code appears immediately.

> **Tip:** Keep the portal open on your phone from the time you leave home so you're not scrambling to find the ticket at the door.

---

## If the QR code won't scan

It happens occasionally. Here's what to try:

- **Maximize your screen brightness** before presenting.
- **Hold the phone a bit farther away** from the scanner (around 15-20 cm / 6-8 inches works well).
- If it still doesn't scan, **give the staff your name and email** — they can look you up in the system and check you in manually.

---

## If you forgot your phone

Not a problem. Staff can find you by your name or email in the system and verify your ticket without the QR code.

---

## Day-of FAQs

**Do I need to print my ticket?**
No. The QR code on your phone screen is all you need.

**Can someone else use my ticket?**
Tickets are personal. Each attendee needs their own ticket.

**What if I'm running late?**
It depends on the experience's late arrival policy. If you're going to be late, contact OMZONE beforehand.

**What can staff see when they scan my QR?**
Only the information needed to check you in: your name and whether your ticket is valid.

glosario.body:
# Glossary

Quick-reference definitions for the terms you'll encounter while using OMZONE.

---

## Experience

The core unit of everything on OMZONE. An experience is a wellness activity you offer — a yoga class, a sound bath, a weekend retreat, a private session. It's the "product" clients browse and book.

---

## Edition

A variation of an experience with different characteristics — for example, the same yoga class offered in a morning format and an evening format. Editions let you present multiple versions without creating completely separate experiences.

---

## Schedule

A specific date and time when an experience is taking place. One experience can have many scheduled sessions. A schedule has a capacity (maximum attendees), an assigned location, and assigned resources (like instructors).

---

## Ticket

Digital proof that a client has a confirmed spot in a session. Each ticket has a unique QR code used for check-in. Tickets are stored in the client portal under **My tickets**.

---

## Reservation

The act of securing a spot in a specific session. When a client completes a purchase for a session, a reservation is created and a ticket is generated.

---

## Order

The transaction record of a client's purchase. An order can contain one or more tickets. It records what was bought, when, at what price, and the payment status.

---

## Pass

A credit-based or time-based membership that lets a client attend multiple sessions without buying each one separately. A session pass has a set number of uses; a time-based pass allows unlimited access within a defined period.

---

## Package

A bundle that includes multiple sessions or items purchased together in one transaction. When a client buys a package, they receive a pass with the corresponding credits or validity.

---

## Publication

The editorial layer of an experience — the story, photos, and formatted content that appears on the public site. A publication is linked to an experience but kept separate so you can update the narrative without changing the commercial details.

---

## Section

A content block within a publication (e.g., a text block, a photo gallery, an instructor bio, a FAQ list). Publications are built by combining sections.

---

## Add-on

An optional extra that clients can purchase alongside an experience — for example, a post-session massage, transport, a starter kit. Add-ons are linked to specific experiences and appear at checkout.

---

## Booking request

An inquiry submitted by a client for an experience that doesn't have fixed pricing or a public schedule (typically private events). The OMZONE team reviews the request and responds with a confirmation or a custom quote.

---

## Assisted sale

A purchase entered manually by an administrator or operator on behalf of a client — for example, when someone pays in person or by phone and you need to log it in the system.

---

## Client portal

The private section of the site accessible to clients after they log in. The portal is where clients find their tickets, passes, purchase history, and profile.

---

## Resource

Anything assignable to a scheduled session — an instructor, a therapist, a piece of equipment, a room. Resources help you manage availability and avoid double-booking.

---

## Location

A physical space where sessions take place. Locations are defined once and reused across schedules.

preguntas-frecuentes.body:
# Frequently asked questions

Answers to the questions we hear most often.

---

## For clients

### How do I book an experience?

Browse the experiences on the site, click the one you want, choose a date and price tier, and follow the checkout steps. You'll need to create an account if you don't have one — it takes about 2 minutes.

### Do I need to print my ticket?

No. Just open your portal, tap **My tickets**, and show the QR code on your phone screen when you arrive.

### What if I lose my ticket?

It's in your portal — you can't lose it. Log in at any time, go to **My tickets**, and your ticket is right there.

### Can I cancel my reservation?

Cancellations depend on the experience's policy. Contact the OMZONE team through the site, and they'll help you based on your situation.

### How do passes work?

A pass gives you a set number of sessions (or unlimited access for a time period). When you book a compatible experience, you choose to use your pass instead of paying separately. Your balance updates automatically.

### Can I share my ticket with someone else?

No. Tickets are personal and tied to your account.

### What if I forget the email I used to sign up?

Contact the OMZONE team with your name and phone number — they can look up your account.

### How do I change my password?

Log in, go to **My profile**, and use the **Change password** option. If you've forgotten your current password, use **Forgot your password?** on the login screen.

---

## For administrators and operators

### How do I create a new experience?

Go to **Experiences** → **New experience**. Fill in the details, add pricing and schedules, create a publication, and set everything to Active. See [Launch a new session](/help/docs/en/casos-de-uso/lanzar-una-sesion) for a full walkthrough.

### Why isn't my experience appearing on the site?

The most common reasons: the experience isn't set to Active, there's no active price tier, or there's no active publication linked. Check all three. See [Common issues](/help/docs/en/referencia/problemas-frecuentes) for details.

### How do I issue a ticket manually?

Go to **Assisted sale** in the admin panel. Search for the client, select the experience and session, choose how they paid, and confirm. A ticket is generated immediately.

### Can I cancel a single ticket without cancelling the whole order?

Yes. Go to **Tickets**, find the specific ticket, and cancel it from the ticket's detail view. The rest of the order remains intact.

### How do I process a refund?

Refunds are handled from **Orders**. Open the relevant order and look for the refund option. The exact process depends on whether the original payment was made through the platform or another method.

### Can I give an operator access to the admin panel?

Yes. Go to **Clients**, find or create their account, and assign the **Operator** role. Operators have access to day-to-day management but not sensitive settings.

### What happens if I deactivate a price tier?

Existing tickets and orders already using that price are not affected. The price tier simply stops appearing for new bookings.

### How do I archive an experience that's no longer being offered?

Go to the experience and set its status to **Inactive** or use the archive option. It will stop showing on the public site but remain in your records.

### How do I reach the OMZONE support team?

Use the contact form on the public site, or reach out through the channel your team uses (email, WhatsApp, etc.).

problemas-frecuentes.body:
# Common issues

A troubleshooting guide in plain language. Find your situation and follow the steps.

---

## My experience isn't showing up on the public site

**Check these in order:**

1. Go to **Experiences** and open the experience.
2. Make sure the status is set to **Active**.
3. Make sure there's at least one active price tier linked to it (**Pricing** tab).
4. Make sure there's a publication linked to it and the publication is set to **Active**.
5. Save and reload the public site.

If it still doesn't appear, try clearing your browser cache.

---

## A session shows "full" but I think there are still spots

1. Go to **Agenda** and open the session.
2. Check the **Capacity** field.
3. Check how many tickets have been issued for that session (go to **Tickets** and filter by that session).
4. If the count is lower than the capacity, there may be a sync issue — contact support.

---

## An order is stuck in Pending status

An order stays in Pending when payment wasn't completed.

1. Go to **Orders** and find the order.
2. If the payment was made by other means (cash, bank transfer), you can manually mark the order as paid.
3. If the payment was attempted but failed, the client needs to try again.
4. If you're unsure, check your payment provider dashboard for the transaction.

---

## A section of the docs isn't loading

If a docs page returns "not found" or the sidebar section is missing:

1. Make sure you're logged into the correct account with docs access.
2. Try navigating to the page directly using the sidebar.
3. Clear your browser cache and reload.
4. If the problem persists, contact the administrator.

---

## An image upload failed

1. Check the file format — accepted formats are JPG, PNG, and WebP.
2. Check the file size — very large files (over a few MB) may be rejected. Compress the image and try again.
3. Try a different browser.
4. If the problem continues, contact support.

---

## A ticket has the wrong status

Ticket statuses update automatically. If a ticket shows an incorrect status:

1. Open the ticket in the **Tickets** section.
2. Review the session date and current status.
3. If the status should have changed (e.g., session passed but ticket still shows "Active"), the system may need a moment to sync — wait a few minutes and refresh.
4. Administrators can update a ticket's status manually from the ticket detail view.

---

## A client can't see their tickets

1. Confirm the client is logged into the correct account (the one used at checkout).
2. Confirm the order status is not **Pending** — tickets are only generated after successful payment.
3. Go to **Clients**, find their account, and check their ticket history directly.
4. If the tickets exist in the system but don't appear for them, ask them to log out and back in.

---

## The QR code won't scan at the door

See [Using your ticket on the day](/help/docs/en/portal/validar-ticket) for full troubleshooting steps.

Short version:
- Maximize screen brightness.
- Hold the phone 15-20 cm from the scanner.
- Staff can look up the client by name or email as a backup.

---

## A client can't reset their password

1. Make sure they're checking the correct email inbox (and spam folder).
2. Have them wait a few minutes and try again.
3. Go to **Clients** in the admin panel, find their account, and manually trigger a password reset from there.

---

## The wrong price is showing on an experience page

1. Go to **Experiences** → **Pricing**.
2. Check which price tiers are active.
3. Deactivate any outdated prices.
4. Confirm the correct price is set to **Active**.
5. Reload the public page.
